title: Staged degradation containment and fix lifecycle for model rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Describe and implement a staged degradation and fix lifecycle for model rollouts that minimizes customer impact across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Current pain: canary regressions surface inconsistently across tenants, and our existing rollback tooling is binary (all-or-nothing) which forces heavy-handed rollbacks or risky canary continuations. This ticket defines a containment-first approach: fast slice quarantine, model-variant fallback, temporary latency trade-offs, and automated patch gating so SRE/SE/CS can coordinate a targeted fix without full-service rollback.
updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff with SRE, Product, and Solutions Engineering. Agreed containment tiers: slice-quarantine, region-fence, and full-rollback. Identified gaps in Dedicated private upgrade playbook for quarantining specific tenant slices.

2026-03-03: Prototype 'slice-quarantine' API + routing rule implemented (branch: feature/slice-quarantine). Demoed cross-env traffic-split for hosted and dedicated pools. Early results: containment reduces affected tokens by ~85% in internal sim.

2026-03-05: Design review with CS and Legal on customer communications during partial quarantines. Decided on templated emails and console banner with opt-in for immediate rollback vs. staged quarantine.

2026-03-07: Integration test found KV cache mismatch after variant fallback in Dedicated when clients pin session IDs. Added reconciliation step to flush per-tenant KV cache during variant swap (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4128).

2026-03-09: Canary failure simulation (model regression seeded) exercised runbook. Observations: fallback to smaller-quantized variant preserved availability but increased token cost by ~37%; acceptable for high-severity incidents. Updated runbook with cost guardrails.

2026-03-11: Working session with Private deployment SME to add offline runbook steps for air-gapped customers (manual traffic redirect + tenant manifests). Created draft docs: https://docs.internal.redwood/rollouts/staged-degradation.md.

2026-03-12: Preparing canary automation for next deploy (automation ticket ENG-48300). Blocking: console UI for rapid slice selection (PM: Lina Morales) — feature requested by CS for better tenant visibility.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Implement slice-quarantine API that supports selecting tenant slices by tag, region, and capacity pool across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
A2: Automated routing rule to divert 100% of traffic for quarantined slice to a stable model-variant or to a degraded-but-available fallback with explicit cost/loss telemetry.
A3: KV cache reconciliation step for per-tenant session pinning to avoid sticky regressions after variant swaps.
A4: Runbook documented with communication templates and role checklist (SRE, SE, CS, Legal), and validated in a simulated canary regression test.
A5: Console support story created and triaged to allow SE/CS to select tenant slices in <5 minutes during incident triage.
A6: Post-release validation: run three simulated regressions with <=10% of tenants requiring full rollback and average mitigation time <20 minutes.
